problem: Entropy-minimization test-time adaptation for VLN (e.g. FSTTA, TENT) blindly increases confidence at every step, so agents become overconfident in wrong actions and accumulate errors, giving small or negative gains under distribution shift.
motivation: VLN policies trained offline degrade in unseen environments, and test-time adaptation without any feedback lacks context on whether a navigation succeeded. Cheap episodic binary human feedback (success/failure), requested only for uncertain episodes, can supply that context without latency or expertise burden.
key_idea: Use sparse episodic success/failure feedback to minimize a mixture (action + pseudo-expert) entropy on successes and maximize it on failures, and let a self-prediction head supply the outcome labels for confident episodes.
insight: Sharpening the action distribution with a one-hot pseudo-expert amplifies the gradient on the selected action, so the same feedback moves the policy more. With human feedback, MEO reaches better SR than TENT/FSTTA with far fewer queries (Active 55.5% vs ~90% on val-unseen). Adding SAL raises DUET REVERIE val-unseen SR from 63.70 to 68.11, and the self-head is 82.19% accurate. Uncertainty-based query selection beats random or consecutive selection and even matches or beats full feedback on SR and RGSPL.
method: Mixture action distribution: q_mix = λ·one-hot(argmax action) + (1-λ)·π_θ; the entropy of q_mix is averaged over episode steps (best λ≈0.4).
Outcome-conditioned mixture entropy loss: L_mix = H'(q_mix) if the episode succeeded, -H'(q_mix) if it failed.

Uncertainty-guided query: after each episode, if the mean action entropy exceeds threshold δ (searched over 0.1/0.2/0.3), ask the human for binary success/failure; otherwise use the agent's own prediction.
Self-prediction head f_φ: initialized at test time, takes the episode-averaged hidden state and predicts success via a sigmoid (>0.5); trained online with BCE on both human and self-generated labels.
Total objective L = L_mix + γ·L_self, updating policy and head after each episode (batch size 1, online streaming), with no ground-truth trajectories.
Plug-in to pretrained policies (HAMT, DUET, BEVBert, GOAT, ETPNav) with no extra pretraining; lightweight, on a single RTX 3090.

setting.backbone: Pretrained VLN policies (HAMT, DUET, GOAT, BEVBert, ETPNav) adapted online at test time, plus a small self-prediction head
setting.training_data: No new offline training; test-time adaptation on the streaming test episodes with episodic binary human feedback (for uncertain episodes) and self-predicted labels
setting.observation: Panoramic RGB (discrete Matterport3D) / RGB-D in the continuous setting, plus language instruction
setting.action_space: Discrete nav-graph viewpoints (REVERIE, R2R); waypoint-based in continuous environments (R2R-CE, via ETPNav/BEVBert)
setting.privileged: Human oracle episodic success/failure labels for uncertain episodes (simulated from ground-truth outcomes) at test time

numbers.extra: test-time adaptation with episodic human feedback + self-active learning; GOAT baseline is own re-implementation

numbers_note: Several baselines (GOAT, TENT, FSTTA) are the authors' re-implementations. The R2R and R2R-CE tables print SR/SPL as integers for some rows. Results are averaged over 3 seeds.
results: ATENA gives large gains on REVERIE: GOAT val-unseen SR goes from 53.82 to 67.66 and test-unseen SR from 57.72 to 62.03 (3rd on the leaderboard), and DUET val-unseen SR from 46.98 to 68.11, versus FSTTA's 54.15. Gains on R2R and R2R-CE are modest, e.g. GOAT R2R val-unseen SPL 67.34→69.30 and BEVBert R2R-CE val-unseen SR 59→60, and FSTTA/TENT often give none or degrade.
limitations: Requires human episodic success/failure feedback, simulated here from ground-truth outcomes; noisy or ambiguous feedback is not tested.
Gains are small on R2R/R2R-CE, where training used dense step-wise supervision, and generalization to other navigation tasks (ObjectNav etc.) is untested.
Sensitive to hyperparameters (δ, λ, learning rates), tuned per benchmark; the self-prediction head is only 82% accurate.
